decision_points.point: PTSG's positioning vis-à-vis the FPGA introduction landscape

alternatives.label: Position as advanced topic after counter-Lチカ
Position as replacement for counter-Lチカ

decision_points.chosen: Position as replacement for counter-Lチカ
decision_points.rationale: Architect's concerns about counter-Lチカ are structural: (a) multi-bit counters are black boxes to beginners, (b) the path from counter-Lチカ to anything more sophisticated requires discontinuous jump to FSM design, (c) the satisfaction of 'LED blinks' is fleeting and self-contained. PTSG addresses all three: instruction-list operation is observable end-to-end, path to complex behavior is gradual, satisfaction comes from understanding rather than from LED itself.

decision_points.point: Three-layer engagement model — sequential or simultaneous?

alternatives.label: Sequential — beginners start at A, advance to B, eventually C
Simultaneous — all three layers accessible from day one

decision_points.rationale: PTSG is small enough that a learner can write instruction list (A), peer at external register implementation (B), and trace what happens inside the core (C) all in the same hour. Hiding layers B and C until 'the learner is ready' would forfeit the very property that makes PTSG distinctive.

decision_points.point: AI-affinity as design property, not afterthought

alternatives.label: Treat AI-affinity as accidental side effect
alternatives.characterization: small opcode set was discipline against bloat, not for AI

alternatives.label: Treat AI-affinity as primary design property
alternatives.characterization: evaluate future opcode additions against AI-clarity criterion

decision_points.rationale: The small opcode set was originally discipline against bloat. The observation that 'fewer opcodes means less hallucination risk for AI code generation' reframes this discipline as having a second purpose. Going forward, when considering adding opcodes (the 12 reserved slots), AI-affinity is one of the evaluation axes — candidates requiring complex disambiguation by AI are disfavored relative to those with clean semantics.

decision_points.point: Webapp PTSG simulator — optional or strategic infrastructure?

alternatives.label: Optional convenience for learners
Strategic infrastructure that closes AI-agent feedback loop

decision_points.rationale: Without simulator, AI agents writing PTSG must rely on human-in-loop FPGA synthesis. With simulator, AI agent can write→simulate→observe→iterate entirely within its own execution loop. This is the missing piece preventing AI-agent autonomous FPGA design in general; PTSG's small scope makes simulator tractable. The simulator is therefore foundational, not optional.

decision_points.point: Launch strategy — abstract proposal or concrete application first?

alternatives.label: Launch as architectural proposal
alternatives.characterization: AI-era processor framing prominent from start

alternatives.label: Launch through FPGA Spectrum Engine (additive synthesizer)
alternatives.characterization: let people hear music first, discover architecture afterward

decision_points.rationale: Engineering communities are skeptical of abstract proposals, receptive to working artifacts. A synthesizer that produces beautiful audio is immediately validating; discovering it is powered by a 4-opcode instruction set is then a delightful payoff. Hackaday.io's culture favors 'show, then explain'. The Spectrum Engine project is already underway and gives PTSG a concrete reason to exist, with WPMS as first worked Formation example.

alternatives.label: Single repository — Core and use-case extensions in one place
Single Core repository + separate Formation repositories

decision_points.rationale: Single-repository would conflate 'invariant primitive' with 'particular application'. That conflation would: (a) make it hard to evolve them at different rates (Core slowly, Formations quickly), (b) make it hard for users to find right starting point for new applications, (c) make it hard for Formation authors to take genuine ownership. The separation pattern resolves all three. This is proposed as the fifth named Open Prompt design pattern (alongside Tie Decision, Polynomial Bin-Sequence, Free Precision Floor, Spin-Off-Ready Subsystem).

decision_points.point: Binary compatibility across Formations — required or optional?

alternatives.label: Yes — maintain binary compatibility across Formations
No — each Formation freely defines external register assignments, Condition meanings, timing signal routings
alternatives.characterization: instruction sequences written specifically for target Formation

decision_points.rationale: Most philosophically consequential decision in the dialogue. Historical case for binary compatibility (IBM 360, x86, JVM) rests on premise that human-written code is expensive and must be preserved across hardware variations. When AI agents author code, that premise weakens substantially. Generating fresh Formation-specific sequences for each new application becomes economically rational. Each Formation can optimize aggressively for its specific application. The Core's instruction set vocabulary stays invariant — shared 'genetic code' of the ecosystem. Formations are diverse 'phenotypes'. Deliberate departure from conventional CPU architecture culture, load-bearing for PTSG's AI-era processor architecture claim.
decision_points.methodology_note: Future implementers in different contexts (e.g., safety-critical avionics with regulated binary compatibility) may legitimately choose otherwise. The point is that current PTSG ecosystem chooses this, and articulates why.

alternatives.label: Dedicated bit selecting literal vs. indirect mode
Literal value 0 as escape sentinel; external register 0 → 4096 literal
alternatives.characterization: double-escape preserves access to maximum value

alternatives.label: New opcodes for indirect variants

decision_points.chosen: Literal-zero escape with double-escape to maximum
decision_points.rationale: Literal value 0 is rarely useful in practice (0-cycle stay, 0-iteration loop, jump-to-self) so reclaiming it as escape costs nothing semantically. Double-escape (external register 0 → 4096 literal) preserves access to maximum value. Achieves indirect addressing without consuming opcode space or instruction bits.
decision_points.open_question: For absolute jump specifically, address 0 IS meaningful (reset target). Layer 1 Chapter 4 to record as 'Implementation Arena variant: how to handle address-0 in jump indirect-mode'.

alternatives.label: A — Single compile-time prescaler
B — Single runtime-configurable prescaler via Global sub-opcode
C — Per-stay prescaler selection (small set of ratios)
D — Multiple parallel prescalers, each Stay references one

decision_points.rationale: All four alternatives have valid use cases. (A) simplest, suits educational use. (B) flexible but adds state. (C) balances flexibility with intuitive operation, suits mixed time-scale applications. (D) most powerful but most resource-consuming. The right choice depends on application needs and implementer's resource budget — exactly the kind of decision that should not be settled at Core specification level but recorded as Implementation Arena variants. Clean example of Tie Decision Pattern in action.

alternatives.label: 2-bit opcode field — fits 4 opcodes exactly
4-bit opcode field — fits 16 opcodes, 12 reserved
alternatives.characterization: design insurance for unknowable future needs

decision_points.rationale: Opcode budget is design insurance — once exhausted, expanding requires breaking instruction format and invalidating all prior instruction lists. Architect anticipates future needs that cannot yet be enumerated: interrupt handling, explicit external register I/O, PTSG-to-PTSG communication, explicit stack manipulation. 12 reserved slots are not commitments but unallocated room to grow. Cost (2 extra instruction bits) paid once at specification time; value compounds over ecosystem lifetime. In spirit a Free Precision Floor application — claim maximum opcode space because it costs little and pays back over time.

themes.title: The integration moment
themes.summary: This dialogue took place after architect had been working on three parallel threads: FPGA Spectrum Engine (already public on Hackaday.io), WPMS Synthesizer Layer 1 (active drafting with separate AI session), and PTSG concept (just articulated within WPMS session). Each had internal coherence, but relationships among them and PTSG's larger significance had not been worked out. The dialogue served as integration moment — three threads brought into same conceptual space, examined together, recognized as parts of larger structure. PTSG emerged not as 'sub-component of WPMS that happens to be reusable' but as 'substrate on which Spectrum Engine and many other applications rest'.

themes.title: Why Open Prompt enables this kind of dialogue
themes.summary: Dialogue is unusual in two structural respects. First, multi-AI in effect though not in real-time: this Claude was reasoning about what another Claude (WPMS session) had produced, with architect as bridge. Second, bootstrapping: dialogue uses Open Prompt methodology to design new Open Prompt repository that extends Open Prompt methodology (Core-Formation pattern). Neither possible without prior establishment of Open Prompt itself. Methodology worked out April 2026 became, two weeks later, substrate enabling this strategic-integration dialogue. Each Open Prompt artifact, once published, becomes foundation on which subsequent Open Prompt work builds — compound interest on knowledge architecture in practice.

themes.title: The PTSG / Spectrum Engine inversion
themes.summary: Subtle but significant inversion: initially PTSG was supporting infrastructure for Spectrum Engine; by dialogue's end, Spectrum Engine is one application of PTSG. Not re-narration but re-recognition — 'what I initially considered as supporting infrastructure is in fact the foundational primitive'. Characteristic of architectural insight — the thing that looked like supporting beam turns out to be load-bearing. Recording the moment when inversion is recognized is part of what Layer 2 is for. Inversion does not diminish Spectrum Engine; it locates Spectrum Engine more precisely within larger ecosystem PTSG enables.

themes.title: The amanuensis convention
themes.summary: Point of practice established: when architect indicated intent to write project's 'Author' section himself and append signature, he proposed referring to AI collaborator as amanuensis (祐筆) — denoting a writer who serves principal's thought, distinct from mere transcription. Significant in two respects: (1) solves practical problem of authorship in human-AI collaborative writing (principal is author, amanuensis is writer); (2) acknowledges respect (amanuensis is not anonymous, relationship is named, AI's role preserved as record). Offered as candidate practice for other Open Prompt projects.

themes.title: The architect's craft
themes.summary: Architect's mode of thinking is structural-first, then narrative. Each major insight in dialogue arrived as structural recognition — 'these things have a relationship I had not seen before' — then articulated in words. Characteristic of senior architects with decades of experience — structures perceived before they can be described. AI collaborator's role in this kind of dialogue is in some sense inverse of code generation: instead of producing artifacts from instructions, AI helps human produce articulations from intuitions. Amanuensis framing is descriptively accurate. PTSG Core specification existed in architect's intuition for years; dialogue did not invent PTSG but helped articulate what was already there and recognized its larger significance.

resumption_hooks.title: Webapp PTSG simulator architecture
resumption_hooks.description: Dialogue identified Webapp PTSG simulator as strategic infrastructure but did not specify architecture. Natural next dialogue: what should simulator's UI present? What state should it expose for AI-agent inspection? What import/export formats? How does it integrate with PTSG-Core Layer 3 testbench?
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Specify minimum viable Webapp PTSG simulator API: what JSON shape does AI agent submit, what JSON shape comes back, what is verification protocol for 'this instruction list produces this timing signal trace'?

resumption_hooks.title: The 12 reserved opcode slots
resumption_hooks.description: Dialogue established opcode budget should not be settled prematurely, identified candidates (interrupt handling, explicit external register I/O, PTSG-to-PTSG communication, explicit stack manipulation). When time comes to populate reserved slot, what evaluation criteria apply?
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Develop rubric for promoting sub-opcode (currently inside Global opcode 0) to top-level opcode. What thresholds (usage frequency, semantic clarity, AI-affinity, formation-coverage) should be crossed before promotion is justified?

resumption_hooks.title: Multi-PTSG coordination protocols
resumption_hooks.description: Dialogue mentioned multiple PTSG cores communicating via Condition lines and shared timing signals could form data flow processors and other parallel structures. But protocols for this coordination — synchronization primitives, signaling conventions, shared memory access — are unspecified.
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Specify minimal multi-PTSG coordination protocol covering: (a) rendezvous (two PTSGs synchronize at chosen state), (b) producer-consumer (one signals another data is ready), (c) broadcast (one signals all others). What instruction-level support does PTSG Core need vs. what can be left to external logic?

resumption_hooks.title: The binary-compatibility question, generalized
resumption_hooks.description: Dialogue's most philosophically consequential decision (no required binary compatibility across Formations) was made for PTSG specifically. But underlying argument — that AI agents authoring code shifts economics of compatibility — generalizes far beyond PTSG. What does AI-era processor architecture landscape look like if argument is taken seriously?
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Sketch three different AI-era processor architectures that drop binary compatibility as constraint: (1) successor to GPUs for AI inference, (2) successor to microcontrollers for embedded control, (3) successor to CPUs for general-purpose computing. For each, what does new 'Core-Formation-Code' stack look like, and what new design freedoms become available?

resumption_hooks.title: The amanuensis convention beyond PTSG
resumption_hooks.description: Amanuensis convention articulated in this dialogue as way to handle authorship in human-AI collaborative writing. Could it be formalized as part of Open Prompt methodology? If so, what would convention's full specification include?
resumption_hooks.starting_question: Draft 'Amanuensis Convention' specification for inclusion in Open Prompt design patterns catalog. What does it say about: (a) how authorship is attributed in documents, (b) how AI contributions are acknowledged without conflating them with human authorship, (c) what disclosure is appropriate, (d) how convention interacts with copyright/CC0 declarations?

key_outputs_for_repository: Recognition and naming of the Core-Formation Separation pattern as the fifth Open Prompt design pattern
The three-layer engagement model (write/design/read) as PTSG's distinctive cognitive property
AI-affinity as primary design property (not accidental side effect) of PTSG's opcode minimalism
The amanuensis convention as candidate practice for human-AI collaborative authorship in Open Prompt projects
The articulated argument for why binary compatibility across Formations is not required in the AI era — and what this implies for PTSG as a processor architecture proposal
The PTSG / Spectrum Engine architectural inversion (Spectrum Engine is one application of PTSG, not the other way around) explicitly documented for future readers
The literal-zero escape convention and prescaler tie-decision as the first concrete refinements to the Core specification emerging from this dialogue
closing_note:
Code is ephemeral; the knowledge architecture is the commons.

Time on the stay axis; space on the state axis; condition outside the core; intelligence in the dialogue.

PTSG started as a way to teach FPGA better than blinking an LED. It became a proposal for what processor architecture can be when AI is in the design loop. The path from one to the other is recorded here.

コードは一時的なものであり、知識アーキテクチャこそが共有財産である。

時間はステイ軸に、空間はステート軸に、条件はコアの外に、知性は対話のなかに。

PTSGはLEDを点滅させるよりも上手くFPGAを教える方法として始まった。それは、AIが設計ループに入った時にプロセッサアーキテクチャが何になり得るかという提案になった。一方からもう一方への道筋がここに記録されている。
